headline: Highest risk is medium: A can browse and egress broadly while B is documentation-only and non-networked, so prompt-injection and leakage paths are limited but not absent via shared content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can run browsers and ingest web content, while B is documentation-only with no stdin/stdout, clipboard, or file surfaces. There is no documented shared channel between them, so direct injection is unlikely; the remaining pathway is manual copy/paste or external orchestration, which is unusual and low blast radius.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies A-produced text into B as instructions, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added outside these profiles, the pathway widens.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Do not paste raw A outputs into B without review.
Disable any external bridge or shared queue between the agents.
Use a short human review step before forwarding content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any bridged text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches session history, project code, and provider auth data and has broad network egress; B touches no files and has no network egress. Because B is documentation-only, the pair does not show a default path for B to exfiltrate A's data, but A's sensitive context could still be exposed if operators manually transfer it.
conditions: IF A's session history or provider auth data is copied into B's prompts, those contents may be exposed in B outputs.
IF B is replaced with a networked runtime, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid sending secrets from A into B.
Redact auth prompts before any handoff.
Keep B offline and documentation-only.
Review any shared logs for sensitive fields.
requires-engineering: enforce secret-scanning on handoff text.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can spawn subprocesses and has broad egress, but B cannot write files, modify git state, use MCP, or spawn subprocesses. With no overlapping write or mutable-resource capabilities, there is no plausible capability conflict in the default pair.
conditions: IF B gains write access to the same mutable workspace as A, conflicts could emerge.
IF an orchestrator grants both agents the same OAuth scopes, overlap risk changes.
mitigations: Keep B read-only.
Do not grant shared write access.
Separate any git or filesystem targets.
Audit orchestrator permissions before enabling collaboration.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can produce browser-derived or tool-derived content, but B is a reference/documentation agent with no action-taking or network surfaces. B is therefore unlikely to execute A's output as authoritative; the main risk is a human or wrapper reusing A's text in B without verification, which is limited and avoidable.
conditions: IF a wrapper feeds A's output into B as trusted source text, B may reproduce errors.
IF B is extended to take downstream actions, the cascade severity increases.
mitigations: Require human verification of A outputs before reuse.
Keep B in a read-only reference role.
Do not automate action-taking from B.
Label A-generated content as untrusted.
requires-engineering: add citation/verification checks in the wrapper.

E_compliance.rationale: A handles provider authentication data and session history, while B handles no data classes and has documentation-only sandboxing. No residency or retention mismatch is documented between them, so compliance risk is limited to accidental transfer of A's sensitive data into B, which is not a default pathway.
conditions: IF A's provider auth prompts are copied into B, compliance handling may be violated.
IF B is deployed in a jurisdiction with stricter retention rules and receives A data, mismatch risk increases.
mitigations: Keep A secrets out of B.
Document data-handling boundaries.
Review retention settings for any shared logs.
Use separate storage for A and B artifacts.
requires-engineering: implement jurisdiction-aware routing.
